37.4 Entities and data model

Figure 37.7 — The person, the assignment and the tables that hang from them.

The diagram has employees at the top right with id, full_name, and phone and cnic marked UK (unique). A "works as" line goes from employees to employee_org_location_assignments, which shows id, employee_id, organization_id, location_id, employment_role_id, user_id, employee_code, has_portal_access and is_active. Over the assignment, four boxes link to it: organizations ("employs"), locations ("is staffed by"), and, as optional links, employment_roles ("role of") and users ("staff login"). Under the assignment, compensation_plans hangs off it ("is paid by"). From employees three more lines go to employee_schedules ("weekly hours": employee_id, location_id, day_of_week, is_working), doctor_availability_overrides ("day exceptions": date, is_available) and employee_leaves ("takes": leave_type, status, total_days).

The relationships in words:

  • Each employee can have several assignments; each assignment belongs to exactly one employee, organization and location. Deleting any of these deletes the assignment (CASCADE). One person has at most one assignment per location (unique employee_id, location_id); the employee code is unique within an organization.
  • An assignment may have one role; deleting the role leaves the assignment without one (SET NULL), which means no permissions. An assignment may have one login; deleting the user clears the link (SET NULL).
  • Schedules, overrides and leave belong to one employee and name one organization and location; deleting the employee or the location deletes them (CASCADE). Schedules are unique per employee, location and weekday; overrides per employee, location and date.
  • Compensation plans belong to the assignment (CASCADE); payroll records belong to the employee and location (Chapter 38).
  • employees.is_active exists but nothing writes it; the active flag that matters is on the assignment. gross_salary on the assignment is deprecated; salary lives in compensation_plans.

The Data model chapter (Chapter 16) lists every column.

37.5 Status lifecycles

37.5.1 Leave request

Figure 37.8 — The states of a leave request.

The diagram has four states. A request enters at pending through POST /leaves. A loop on pending shows PATCH /leaves/:id (edit). From pending, PATCH …/approve leads to approved, PATCH …/reject to rejected and PATCH …/cancel to cancelled. From approved, PATCH …/cancel leads to cancelled. Approved, rejected and cancelled all lead to the end marker.

  • pending — filed, can be edited, approved, rejected or cancelled; blocks overlapping requests.
  • approved — counts in the summary and blocks overlapping requests; can still be cancelled.
  • rejected — final; does not block.
  • cancelled — final; does not block.

Any other change is refused with 400.

37.5.2 Employee (assignment) status

Figure 37.9 — Active, inactive and deleted.

The diagram shows an employee entering Active through POST /employees. PATCH /employees/:id/status with isActive false moves Active to Inactive; with isActive true it moves back. From either state, DELETE /employees/:id leads to Deleted and the end marker.

The status is the assignment's is_active flag at one location; the same person can be active at one location and inactive at another. Deleted is not a stored state: the rows are gone.

37.6 Connections to other modules

  • Appointments and queue (Chapters 29 and 30). Doctors are active assignments at the location; weekly schedules drive booking. Overrides and leave are not read.
  • Access control (Chapters 11 and 57). The role and portal flag on the assignment decide what a staff login may do; changes bump the access version.
  • Authentication (Chapter 56). Sign-in lists organizations and locations from active assignments with portal access.
  • Commissions (Chapter 35). Compensation plans per assignment; salary updates create plan versions.
  • Payroll (Chapter 38). Generated for active assignments; reads the plan.
  • Subscriptions (Chapter 45). The User Admin path counts logins against the plan's limit; writes are refused in read-only mode.

37.7 Limitations and known gaps

  • No way to add an existing person at a second location or organization; the phone check blocks it.
  • Employee creation is not one transaction: if the login email is already taken, the person record is already saved, and a retry fails on the phone number.
  • A duplicate CNIC (and a duplicate phone on edit) returns a generic 500 instead of a clear message.
  • The employee code is "number of assignments + 1"; after deletions it can repeat an existing code and the save fails.
  • Availability overrides and approved leave do not affect booking.
  • Leave can only be filed by managers (leave.approve); there is no self-service, no entitlement and no attendance.
  • Payslips and CSV show the designation as empty, because it is read from the person record instead of the assignment (Chapter 38).
  • Overlapping weekly hours of one person at two locations are not checked.
  • Employee changes are not written to the general audit log.

37.8 Owner's FAQ

Can the same doctor work at two of our branches? The data model supports it (one assignment per location), but there is no screen or endpoint to add the second assignment today.

Why does "Add Employee" say the phone number already exists when the person is new to my clinic? Phone numbers are unique across the whole Platform. The person may already be registered by another clinic.

What is the difference between deactivating and deleting? Deactivating keeps everything and blocks login, booking and payroll at this location. Deleting removes the person and their schedules, leave, overrides, plans and payroll records, and is refused if they work elsewhere or are still referenced.

Can a receptionist see staff salaries? Not with the default role; only the Admin holds employees.view.

If I mark a doctor on leave, will reception be stopped from booking them? No. Leave and availability overrides are recorded but not checked by booking.

How does a staff member get a login? Turn on Portal Access when adding or editing them, or use User Admin → "Staff (existing employee)". Their permissions come from their role.

Where is a salary stored? In compensation_plans, as a dated version per assignment, in paisa.

Chapter 38 — Payroll

This chapter describes the Payroll module of the Platform: how a clinic turns each staff member's pay terms into one monthly payroll record, tracks it until it is paid, and exports it as a payslip or a spreadsheet. It is written for the product owner, who needs to know exactly how base salary and doctor commission are combined and which gaps remain. Payroll reads pay terms from the Employees module (Chapter 37) and commission from the Commissions module (Chapter 35).

38.1 What this module is for

A payroll record is one month's pay for one employee at one location. It stores a base salary, a commission amount and their total, all in integer paisa, plus a status (pending, paid, on hold), the payment method and reference once paid, and notes. There is at most one record per employee, location and month.

Records come from three sources: the automatic month-end job, the Generate Payroll action (all employees of the active location for a chosen month), and Create Payroll (one record typed in by hand).

Who uses it: the Admin and the owner. No other system role (Doctor, Receptionist, Assistant, Accountant) holds the permission by default. The permission payroll.manage is marked high-risk in the role editor.

Where it appears: the sidebar item Payroll (key nav.payroll, route /payroll, needs payroll.manage) in the Team section. The employee detail page also has a Payroll tab for the same permission. The whole module sits behind the feature hr.payroll ("Payroll", enabled by default).

38.2 Screens

Figure 38.1 — The Location Payroll page (screenshot pending).

The page title is "Location Payroll" with the subtitle "Manage monthly payroll for this location". In the header are a month selector, a year selector (current year minus two to plus two), a Create Payroll button and a Generate Payroll button. Under the header, four cards summarise the chosen month: Total Payroll (amount and "N employees"), Paid Amount ("N paid records"), Pending Amount ("N pending records") and On Hold ("Records on hold"). A heading "Records for October 2026" introduces a paged table with the columns Employee, Period, Amount (with a small "commission …" line when the record includes commission), Status (Pending, Paid or On Hold badge), Paid On, Method and an actions column. Actions are Mark as Paid (hidden once paid), an edit icon button ("Edit payroll") and a delete icon button ("Delete payroll"). An empty month shows "No payroll records found."

Figure 38.2 — The Generate Payroll dialog (screenshot pending).

The dialog says "Generate payroll records for all active employees at this location" and offers a Month and a Year selector and a note that existing records for the same month are skipped. After it runs, a toast lists how many records were created, how many already existed and the names of employees with no salary set.

Figure 38.3 — The dialog for one payroll record (screenshot pending).

The dialog has Employee (a searchable list when creating, read-only when editing), Month, Year, Amount, Status (Pending, Paid, On Hold) and Notes ("Reason for this payroll (e.g. mid-month joiner, bonus adjustment)…"). Choosing an employee pre-fills the amount with their current salary.

Figure 38.4 — The Mark Salary as Paid dialog (screenshot pending).

The dialog "Mark Salary as Paid" asks for Payment Method (cash, bank transfer or cheque), Reference Number ("Transaction ID or reference") and Notes (optional). On success a toast confirms the payment.

Figure 38.5 — The Payroll tab of an employee (screenshot pending).

The tab shows "Payroll History" with a Generate This Month button (when this month has no record and the person has a salary or a commission plan), the same table without the Employee column, or an empty state "No payroll records yet — Generate payroll to track monthly salaries" with a Generate Payroll button. Its Generate button opens the same dialog as the main page, which generates for the whole location, not only this person.

38.3 Features

38.3.1 Generate payroll for a month

Status: [Implemented]

What it does. Creates one pending payroll record for every active employee of the active location who has something to be paid for the chosen month, and settles that employee's unsettled commission into it.

How the user does it.

  1. Open Payroll and choose the month and year.
  2. Click Generate Payroll, check the month and year, and confirm.
  3. Read the toast: records created, records skipped, employees with no salary.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. For each active employee the Platform skips anyone who already has a record that month. Otherwise it takes the base salary from the pay plan in force at the end of the month, adds all the doctor's commission earned but not yet paid out, and saves one record. An employee with neither salary nor commission is listed as "no salary".

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /payroll/generate with { month, year } → PayrollService.generate → generateForLocation. The month may not be in the future in the location's clinic calendar (400 "Cannot generate payroll for future months"). All work for the location runs in one transaction on a query runner; any error rolls back the whole location. Per active assignment (EmployeesService.getActiveAssignmentsByLocation) the steps are the same as in the month-end job drawn in Figure 38.6 and described in 38.3.2.

Rules and validations.

  • Month 1–12, year at least 2020 (body); not in the future.
  • Unique per employee, location and month (database constraint and a prior read).
  • Base salary = base_salary_paisa of the compensation plan in force on the last day of the month, else on the first day; if the assignment has no plan at all, the deprecated gross_salary is used.
  • Commission = sum of the assignment's unsettled commission_entries created before the end of the month's last clinic day (location timezone), locked FOR UPDATE. A net-negative sum is not settled and is carried to a later month; the record then has commission 0.
  • Total = base + commission; salary_amount (rupees) mirrors the total.
  • Nothing to pay (both zero) → no record; the name goes into noSalary.
  • Records are created pending, with created_by = the user.

Who can do it. payroll.manage, feature hr.payroll. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Reads employee_org_location_assignments, employees, compensation_plans, commission_entries. Writes payroll_records, commission_settlements, commission_entries.settlement_id.

Effects on other modules. Commission becomes "settled" on the earnings pages (Chapter 35).

Error cases. 400 "Cannot generate payroll for future months"; 400 validation messages for month or year; 403 NO_PERMISSION; 402 SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED in read-only mode.

Technical references: backend/src/payroll/payroll.service.ts · PayrollService.generate, generateForLocation · web-app/src/features/employees/components/GeneratePayrollModal.tsx

38.3.2 Month-end automatic generation

Status: [Implemented]

What it does. On the first day of every month the Platform generates payroll for the month that just ended, for every active location of every organization.

How the user does it. Nothing to do. Open Payroll afterwards and select the previous month. Records made this way have no created_by.

Figure 38.6 shows the job, including the commission settlement.

Figure 38.6 — The month-end job, with commission settlement, per location and per assignment.

The diagram has six participants: Scheduler, PayrollService, EmployeesService, CompensationPlanVersions, CommissionSettlements and PostgreSQL. In step 1 the scheduler calls runMonthEndPayroll at 05:00 server time on the 1st. In step 2 the service loads every active location. A first box, "loop: each active location, in its own transaction", contains the rest. Step 3 asks EmployeesService for the active assignments of the location and step 4 returns them with their employees. A second box, "loop: each assignment", opens with step 5, a check whether a record for this employee, location and month exists. An "alt" box has two branches. If a record exists (step 6) it is counted as skipped. Otherwise step 7 asks CompensationPlanVersions for the plan in force on the last day of the month, else the first day, and step 8 returns the plan with base_salary_paisa. Step 9 calls lockUnsettled on CommissionSettlements for entries before the period end with a row lock and step 10 returns the entry ids and their total. A nested "alt" box then decides: if base and commission are both zero (step 11) the name is added to the no-salary list; otherwise step 12 inserts a PENDING payroll record whose total is base plus commission, and an optional step 13, taken only when entries were found and their total is not negative, creates a PENDING settlement and sets settlement_id on the entries. Step 14, after the loops, commits the location, or rolls back only that location.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. It is the same work as manual generation, run for every clinic in one go. If one clinic fails, the others still run. Running it twice, or after a manual generation, is safe because existing records are skipped.

Behind the scenes — technically. PayrollService.runMonthEndPayroll, decorated @Cron('0 5 1 * *', { name: 'month-end-payroll' }) with no timezone option, so it fires at 05:00 server time on the 1st. The code comment above it says "00:05", which is wrong; the expression means 05:00 (the same conflict is noted in the scheduled-jobs appendix). The month is computed from the server's own new Date() (previous month, December of the previous year in January), not from each location's timezone. It loads locations with is_active = true (without checking that the organization is active or that hr.payroll is enabled), calls generateForLocation(…, userId = null) for each in a try/catch, and logs totals generated and skipped. It runs where scheduled jobs run (the worker or all-in-one process).

Rules and validations. Same as 38.3.1, except there is no future-month check and no user.

Who can do it. The scheduler; no permission.

Data read and written. As in 38.3.1.

Effects on other modules. As in 38.3.1.

Error cases. A location error is logged ("Month-end payroll failed for location …") and skipped; there is no in-app notification.

Technical references: backend/src/payroll/payroll.service.ts · PayrollService.runMonthEndPayroll · no web-app use

38.3.3 Create a payroll record by hand

Status: [Implemented]

What it does. Adds one record for a chosen employee and month, for example for a mid-month joiner or a bonus.

How the user does it.

  1. Click Create Payroll.
  2. Pick the employee, month, year, amount, status and notes; submit.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. The amount you type is stored as the base salary with zero commission. This record does not settle any commission.

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /payroll → PayrollService.createManual: refuses a duplicate (400 "A payroll record already exists for this employee and period"), then inserts with base_salary_paisa = total_paisa = rupee amount converted to paisa (at most 2 decimals), commission_paisa = 0, status from the request (default pending) and the notes.

Rules and validations.

  • Month 1–12, year at least 2020, amount at least 0.
  • The server does not check that the employee has an assignment at this location, nor that the month is not in the future.
  • Choosing status "Paid" here records no payment method, no paid date and no settlement change.

Who can do it. payroll.manage, feature hr.payroll. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Reads payroll_records. Writes payroll_records.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 400 "A payroll record already exists for this employee and period"; 400 "Amount must have at most 2 decimals".

Technical references: backend/src/payroll/payroll.service.ts · PayrollService.createManual · web-app/src/features/employees/components/CreateEditPayrollModal.tsx

38.3.4 View payroll for a month or for one employee

Status: [Implemented]

What it does. Lists the month's records of the location with a summary, or all records of one employee.

How the user does it.

  1. Open Payroll and pick a month and year, or open an employee's Payroll tab.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. The four summary cards add up the month's records by status.

Behind the scenes — technically. GET /payroll/location?month&year → PayrollService.findByLocation returns the records (with the employee) and a summary: total employees, total amount, paid, pending and on-hold counts, paid and pending amounts and the paisa split into base and commission. A month outside 1–12 or a year outside 2000–2100, or a non-number, returns 400 "month must be 1–12" / "year must be a four-digit year". GET /payroll/employee/:id → findByEmployee returns the person's records in the organization, newest first.

Rules and validations.

  • The summary uses the rupee amounts; records created before the paisa breakdown fall back to those.
  • The location list is scoped to the active location; the per-employee list covers every location of the organization.

Who can do it. payroll.manage, feature hr.payroll. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Reads payroll_records, employees.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 400 "month must be 1–12"; 400 "year must be a four-digit year".

Technical references: backend/src/payroll/payroll.controller.ts · payrollPeriod, PayrollService.findByLocation · web-app/src/features/employees/pages/PayrollPage.tsx

38.3.5 Mark a record as paid

Status: [Implemented]

What it does. Records that the salary was paid, how, and with what reference, and marks the linked commission settlement as paid.

How the user does it.

  1. In the table, click Mark as Paid.
  2. Choose Payment Method, enter a Reference Number and optional Notes, and confirm.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. The record becomes paid with the time, the method and who paid it. In the same step the commission that was bundled into it is marked paid, so it can never be released again.

Behind the scenes — technically. PATCH /payroll/:id/mark-paid → PayrollService.markPaid, one transaction: loads the record in the organization, refuses a paid one (400 "Payroll already marked as paid"), sets status paid, paid_at = now, payment_method (cash, bank_transfer or cheque), payment_reference, paid_by and notes (the notes field is replaced, also by empty), then CommissionSettlements.markPaid sets the settlement to PAID.

Rules and validations.

  • Payment method is required and must be one of the three values; reference and notes are optional text.
  • An on-hold record can be paid.
  • No money moves: the Platform records the payout, it does not make it, and it posts nothing to the general ledger or expenses.

Who can do it. payroll.manage, feature hr.payroll. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Writes payroll_records, commission_settlements.

Effects on other modules. Settled commission appears as settled on the earnings pages (Chapter 35). The payroll cost report counts records by month (Chapter 36).

Error cases. 400 "Payroll already marked as paid"; 404 "Payroll record not found"; toast "Failed to mark as paid".

Technical references: backend/src/payroll/payroll.service.ts · PayrollService.markPaid · web-app/src/features/employees/components/MarkPaidModal.tsx

38.3.6 Put a record on hold

Status: [Partial] — the endpoint and the edit dialog's status field work, but no button calls mark-on-hold.

What it does. Marks a record as on hold, for example while a dispute is resolved.

How the user does it.

  1. Click the edit icon on a record, set Status to On Hold and save.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. On hold changes only the label and the summary counts. The commission stays tied to the record.

Behind the scenes — technically. PATCH /payroll/:id/mark-on-hold → PayrollService.markOnHold refuses a paid record (400 "Cannot put a paid payroll record on hold"). A client function for it exists in payroll.api.ts, but no hook or screen uses it. The edit dialog uses PATCH /payroll/:id (38.3.7).

Rules and validations. Not allowed on paid records.

Who can do it. payroll.manage, feature hr.payroll. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Writes payroll_records.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 400 "Cannot put a paid payroll record on hold"; 404.

Technical references: backend/src/payroll/payroll.service.ts · PayrollService.markOnHold · web-app/src/features/employees/services/payroll.api.ts

38.3.7 Edit a payroll record

Status: [Implemented]

What it does. Changes the amount, month, year, status or notes of a record.

How the user does it.

  1. Click the edit icon ("Edit payroll"), change fields and save.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. The amount you edit is the total. Commission already inside the record stays as it is, and the difference is treated as base salary.

Behind the scenes — technically. PATCH /payroll/:id → PayrollService.update: for a new amount, total = paisa(amount); the amount may not be below commission_paisa; base_salary_paisa = total − commission. Month and year changes rebuild the period label. The save maps a unique-key clash (23505) to 400.

Rules and validations.

  • Amount at least 0, at most 2 decimals; month 1–12; year at least 2020.
  • Editing is allowed in any status, including paid.
  • Setting the status to "paid" here does not set the paid date, method or reference and does not mark the settlement paid (see 38.7).

Who can do it. payroll.manage, feature hr.payroll. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Writes payroll_records.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 400 "The amount cannot be below the commission already in this payroll"; 400 "A payroll record already exists for this employee and period"; 404 "Payroll record not found".

Technical references: backend/src/payroll/payroll.service.ts · PayrollService.update · web-app/src/features/employees/components/CreateEditPayrollModal.tsx

38.3.8 Delete a payroll record

Status: [Implemented]

What it does. Deletes a record and returns its commission to the unsettled pool, unless commission was already paid out.

How the user does it.

  1. Click the delete icon ("Delete payroll") and accept the browser confirmation "Delete the payroll record for … ? This cannot be undone."

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. Deleting an unpaid record frees its commission so the next generation picks it up again. A record that paid out commission cannot be deleted.

Behind the scenes — technically. DELETE /payroll/:id → PayrollService.remove, one transaction: CommissionSettlements.release locks the settlement; PENDING → clears settlement_id on its entries and deletes the settlement; PAID → 400; none → nothing. Then the record is removed. The confirmation uses the browser's window.confirm, not the project's confirmation dialog.

Rules and validations. A paid record with no commission settlement (zero commission) can be deleted.

Who can do it. payroll.manage, feature hr.payroll. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Deletes payroll_records, commission_settlements; updates commission_entries.

Effects on other modules. The commission appears as pending again on the earnings pages.

Error cases. 400 "This payroll paid out commission and cannot be deleted"; 404 "Payroll record not found".

Technical references: backend/src/payroll/payroll.service.ts · PayrollService.remove · web-app/src/features/employees/components/PayrollTable.tsx

38.3.9 Export a month as CSV

Status: [Partial] — the endpoint works; no button in the web app calls it.

What it does. Returns a CSV file for one month at the active location.

How the user does it. Not available in the web app. The API can be called directly.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. One row per record with base salary, commission, gross, deductions, net, status, method and paid date.

Behind the scenes — technically. GET /payroll/export?month&year → PayrollExportService.generatePayrollSummaryCsv with the same month and year validation (400). Columns: Employee Name, Designation, Base Salary, Commission, Gross Pay, Deductions, Net Pay, Status, Payment Method, Paid Date. Deductions are always 0.00 and net equals gross. Designation reads a field the employee record does not have, so the column is empty. Response type text/csv, file name payroll-<year>-<month>.csv.

Rules and validations. Active location only. Amounts come from paisa.

Who can do it. payroll.manage, feature hr.payroll. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Reads payroll_records, employees.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 400 "month must be 1–12" / "year must be a four-digit year".

Technical references: backend/src/payroll/payroll-export.service.ts · PayrollExportService.generatePayrollSummaryCsv · none

38.3.10 Payslip PDF

Status: [Partial] — the endpoint works; no button in the web app calls it.

What it does. Returns a one-page A4 PDF payslip for one record.

How the user does it. Not available in the web app.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. The slip shows the period, the employee, base salary, commission, gross pay, deductions (always zero), net pay, status, payment method and paid date.

Behind the scenes — technically. GET /payroll/:id/payslip-pdf → PayrollExportService.generatePayslipPdf, built with pdf-lib and Helvetica (Latin text only). 38.4 Entities and data model

Figure 38.7 — The payroll record and the tables that feed it.

The diagram has payroll_records at the top, showing id, employee_id, organization_id, location_id, month, year, base_salary_paisa, commission_paisa, total_paisa and status. Three lines come into it from employees ("is paid"), organizations ("owns") and locations ("pays at"). A one-to-one optional line labelled "pays out" connects it to commission_settlements (assignment_id, payroll_record_id, total_paisa, status). commission_settlements has an optional one-to-many line "settles" to commission_entries (assignment_id, settlement_id, amount_paisa), and a line "is settled" from employee_org_location_assignments (shown only as a relationship). The same assignment has a line "is paid by" to compensation_plans (type, base_salary_paisa).

The relationships in words:

  • Each payroll record belongs to one employee, one organization and one location. Deleting any of them deletes the record (ON DELETE CASCADE).
  • A record is unique per employee, location, month and year.
  • A record has at most one commission settlement; the settlement's link to the record is ON DELETE RESTRICT, so a record that has one cannot be removed by a plain database delete. The service releases and deletes the settlement first.
  • A settlement groups entries of one assignment; entries only point to it and are never changed otherwise.
  • The base salary is copied from the compensation plan at generation time. Later plan changes do not change existing records.
  • Columns: period_label (for example "October 2026"), salary_amount (rupee decimal mirror of the total), the three paisa columns, status, paid_at, payment_method, payment_reference, paid_by, notes, created_by (empty for the job).

38.5 Status lifecycles

Figure 38.8 — The states of a payroll record.

The diagram has three stored states and a "deleted" end state. A record enters pending through POST /payroll/generate, the month-end job or POST /payroll. From pending, PATCH …/mark-paid leads to paid, and PATCH …/mark-on-hold or a PATCH /payroll/:id with a status change leads to on_hold. From on_hold, PATCH …/mark-paid leads to paid, and a status edit leads back to pending. Pending and on_hold lead to deleted through DELETE /payroll/:id; paid leads to deleted only when no commission was paid out. Deleted leads to the end marker.

  • pending — generated and waiting for payment; its commission settlement, if any, is PENDING.
  • on_hold — set aside; nothing else changes.
  • paid — payment method, reference, date and payer recorded; the settlement is PAID. Editing is still possible.

38.6 Connections to other modules

  • Employees (Chapter 37). Payroll runs over active assignments and reads their plans; the employee page has a Payroll tab.
  • Commissions (Chapter 35). Settlement lock, mark paid and release.
  • Dashboard and reports (Chapter 36). The payroll and staff-cost reports and the finance overview read payroll_records by month.
  • Subscriptions (Chapter 45). Read-only mode refuses generation, edits and payments with 402.
  • Scheduled jobs (Chapter 63). The month-end job is one of the timed jobs.

38.7 Limitations and known gaps

  • The month-end job's code comment says 00:05; the schedule is 05:00 server time, and the month is taken from server time, not from each location's timezone.
  • The job does not check that the organization is active or that hr.payroll is on.
  • Marking a record paid through the edit dialog's Status field does not pay the commission settlement; a later delete would then release the commission back to the pool.
  • Manual creation does not check the assignment or the month, and a hand-made record carries no commission.
  • Payslip PDF and CSV export have no button.
  • On-hold has no button; the delete confirmation is a browser dialog.
  • Designation is empty on exports.
  • No deductions, tax, overtime or unpaid-leave handling; no general-ledger posting for salary payment.
  • Payroll changes are not written to the general audit log.

38.8 Owner's FAQ

When does payroll run by itself? At 05:00 server time on the 1st of each month, for the month that just ended, at every active location.

What if I generate manually first? Safe: existing records are skipped, so the job and manual runs never double up.

A doctor is paid only commission. Will they get a record? Yes, if they have unsettled commission of zero or more. A commission-only doctor with no earnings gets none and appears in the "no salary" list.

What happens to commission reversed after payroll was paid? It becomes a negative entry that is settled with the next payroll, reducing it.

Can I delete a paid record? Only if it paid out no commission.

Can I change the amount after generating? Yes, with the edit icon; it may not go below the commission in the record.

Can I get a payslip? The endpoint exists, but the web app has no button yet.

Is the unique rule per person or per branch? Per person per branch per month: a doctor at two branches gets two records.

Chapter 39 — Inventory

This chapter describes the Inventory module of the Platform: how a clinic keeps a list of its supplies, tracks how much of each it holds, buys more from suppliers through purchase orders, and defines kits of materials used per procedure. It is written for the product owner, who needs to know exactly what works today and where the module stops. Inventory is a per-location module; it has a complete set of screens, but no sidebar entry, and several of its write paths carry an unverified risk that is explained in full.

39.1 What this module is for

The module keeps a stock list for each location. Every change of quantity is recorded as a stock movement, so the clinic can always see who changed what, when and why. Staff can:

  • add items (gloves, composite, anaesthetic cartridges…) with a unit, cost, reorder level and expiry date;
  • correct stock by hand, write off wastage, record transfers and returns;
  • keep a list of suppliers and raise purchase orders, then receive the goods into stock;
  • define consumption templates (kits of items used for a procedure).

Who uses it: the Admin role (all actions) and the Assistant role (view only). Doctor, Receptionist and Accountant have no inventory permission by default.

Where it appears: no sidebar entry. The page /inventory exists and is protected by inventory.view, but web-app/src/features/access/nav/nav.registry.ts has no item for it, and no other screen links to it. Users reach it only by typing the address. The component that would record materials used on a patient (ConsumptionRecorder) is exported but not placed on any screen, so the consultation and patient screens offer no link either.

Two features exist: inventory.core ("Inventory", off by default) gates every permission of the module; inventory.alerts ("Inventory Alerts", off by default) only switches on the daily alert job.

39.2 Screens

The page title is "Inventory Management" with the subtitle "Track supplies, suppliers, purchase orders and consumption". Without an active location it shows "Select a location first". Above four tabs (Items, Suppliers, Purchase Orders, Templates) sits a strip of five tiles: Total Items, Total Value (stock × cost price), Low Stock, Expiring (within 30 days) and Out of Stock.

Figure 39.1 — Inventory, Items tab (screenshot pending).

The Items tab has a search box ("Search name or SKU…"), a category filter ("All categories"), two toggle buttons Low Stock and Expiring, and an Add Item button for users with inventory.stock.adjust. The table shows Name, SKU, Category, Stock (for example "12 / 10 pieces", coloured red when at or below the reorder level, amber up to twice that level, green above, or "Out of stock"), Unit Price and Expiry (a red "Expired" badge or a warning when within 30 days). A three-dot menu per row offers Edit item, Adjust stock, View movements and Deactivate (the last asks a browser confirmation "Deactivate "…"?"). Pages of 20 with Previous / Next. The Add Item / edit form is a dialog with Name, SKU, Category, Initial Stock (new items only), Unit, Cost Price, Reorder Level, Expiry Date, a Billable to patient switch with Selling Price, and Description.

Figure 39.2 — Item detail sheet and the Adjust Stock dialog (screenshot pending).

Clicking a row opens a side sheet with the item name, SKU, Category, Unit, Cost Price, Selling Price, Expiry, Current Stock against the reorder level, an Adjust Stock button and a "Stock Movements" table (Date, Type, Qty, After, Notes) of the ten most recent movements. The Adjust Stock dialog, titled "Adjust Stock — ", offers Reason (Manual Adjustment, Wastage, Return to Supplier, Transfer In, Transfer Out), Quantity, Direction (Increase or Decrease, for manual adjustments), Batch Number and Expiry Date (for incoming stock), Notes (required for manual adjustment and wastage), and a preview "Current: 12 → New: 9".

Figure 39.3 — Inventory, Suppliers tab (screenshot pending).

The Suppliers tab lists Name, Contact Person, Phone, Email and City, with Add Supplier for users with inventory.po.manage and a row menu to edit or deactivate. The supplier dialog has Name (required), Contact Person, Phone, Email, City, Address, Website and Notes ("Payment terms, delivery schedule…").

Figure 39.4 — Inventory, Purchase Orders tab with its dialogs (screenshot pending).

The Purchase Orders tab has status buttons All, Draft, Ordered, Partial and Received (no Cancelled filter) and Create PO. The table shows PO #, Supplier, Order Date, Expected, Items, Total and Status. The "Create Purchase Order" dialog takes a supplier, Expected Delivery, items with Qty and Unit Price, Tax Rate (%) and Notes, and shows Subtotal, Tax and Total. Clicking a PO opens a sheet with its status badge, the lines (Item, Ordered, Received, Unit Price, Total) and buttons by status: Mark as Ordered and Cancel for a draft, Receive Items (or Receive More Items) for an ordered or partly received PO. The "Receive Items — PO-…" dialog asks per line for "Receiving now", Batch # and Expiry.

Figure 39.5 — Inventory, Templates tab (screenshot pending).

The Templates tab lists Template, Procedure, Appointment Type and Items, with Add Template, edit and deactivate actions for users with inventory.stock.adjust. The template dialog has a name ("Root Canal Kit"), a procedure ("Root Canal"), "Appointment Type (for auto-matching)" and "Add Items to Kit" with quantity and notes per item.

39.3 Features

39.3.1 Browse stock and see stock health

Status: [Partial] — works; reachable only by typing /inventory (no sidebar entry).

What it does. Lists the active items at the active location with search, category, low-stock and expiring filters, and shows five stock-health tiles.

How the user does it.

  1. Type the address /inventory.
  2. Search, pick a category, or toggle Low Stock / Expiring.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. Low stock means more than zero but at or below the reorder level. Expiring means the item's nearest expiry date is within 30 days (already expired items count too). Total value is quantity times the last cost price.

Behind the scenes — technically. GET /inventory/items (InventoryService.findAll, paged, default 20, ILIKE on name and SKU) and GET /inventory/items/stats (getStats). Separate endpoints GET /inventory/items/low-stock, /expiring?daysAhead=30 and /out-of-stock exist; the web app has hooks for two of them but no component calls them. GET /inventory/categories fills the category filter.

Rules and validations.

  • Active location and active items only.
  • The 30-day window uses the server's date, not the location's; the per-item expiryAlertDays setting is stored but not used.
  • The search box is not debounced; each keystroke queries.

Who can do it. inventory.view, feature inventory.core. Default: Admin, Assistant.

Data read and written. Reads inventory_items, inventory_categories.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 403 NO_PERMISSION; the page shows "No items found" for an empty result (no separate filtered-empty message).

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/controllers/inventory.controller.ts · InventoryService.findAll, getStats · web-app/src/features/inventory/components/ItemsTab.tsx

39.3.2 Add, edit and deactivate an item

Status: [Partial] — adding without stock, editing and deactivating work; adding with an initial stock goes through the stock-movement path whose foreign-key risk is described in 39.3.4 ([Unverified]).

What it does. Creates a stock item at the active location, edits its details, or hides it (soft delete).

How the user does it.

  1. Click Add Item, fill the dialog and save; or choose Edit item in the row menu.
  2. To remove, choose Deactivate and confirm.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. A new item starts at zero. If an initial stock is entered, an "initial stock" movement is recorded right after. Editing can never change the quantity; only movements can.

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /inventory/items → InventoryService.create (SKU uniqueness check per organization, save with currentStock = 0, then adjustStock with INITIAL_STOCK when initialStock > 0; these are two separate steps, not one transaction). PATCH /inventory/items/:id → update (drops currentStock from the payload). DELETE /inventory/items/:id → deactivate (sets isActive = false).

Rules and validations.

  • Name, unit, cost price and initial stock (0 or more) are required by the API; reorder level defaults to 10, reorder quantity to 50, expiry alert days to 30.
  • SKU must be unique within the organization (checked in code, not by a database constraint).
  • Units: pieces, boxes, pairs, rolls, bottles, packets, cartridges, tubes, ml, gm, kg, liters.
  • "Billable to patient" and the selling price are stored, but no billing screen uses them.

Who can do it. inventory.stock.adjust (implies inventory.view), feature inventory.core. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Writes inventory_items (and stock_movements for initial stock).

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 409 "An item with SKU "GLV-M-001" already exists"; 404 "Inventory item not found"; in the dialog "Name is required".

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/services/inventory.service.ts · InventoryService.create, update, deactivate · web-app/src/features/inventory/components/ItemFormDialog.tsx

39.3.3 Manage categories

Status: [Partial] — the API supports create, rename and deactivate; the web app only lists categories, so there is no way to create one from a screen.

What it does. Groups items (for example "Consumables", "Anaesthetics") for filtering.

How the user does it. Only pick an existing category in the item form or the filter. No screen creates categories, and the default-category seeding function is never called, so a new organization has none.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. Categories are shared by all locations of an organization.

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /inventory/categories, GET, PATCH /inventory/categories/:id, DELETE (deactivate) → InventoryCategoryService. seedDefaults exists but has no caller. The web hooks useCreateCategory, useUpdateCategory, useDeleteCategory are not used by any component.

Rules and validations. Organization-wide; deactivated categories are hidden. Deleting a category row in the database sets items' category to null.

Who can do it. View: inventory.view; change: inventory.stock.adjust. Feature inventory.core.

Data read and written. inventory_categories.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 404 "Category not found".

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/services/inventory-category.service.ts · InventoryCategoryService · web-app/src/features/inventory/hooks/useCategories.ts

39.3.4 Adjust stock and keep the movement history

Status: [Unverified] — the logic is complete and the screen calls it, but the code stores the signed-in user's id in stock_movements.performedBy, a column with a foreign key to employees. User ids and employee ids are different records on the Platform, so the insert is expected to fail with a database error. Not run or tested.

What it does. Changes an item's quantity for a stated reason and records the change as a stock movement with the stock before and after.

How the user does it.

  1. Choose Adjust stock in the row menu, or Adjust Stock in the item sheet.
  2. Pick the Reason, enter the Quantity (and Direction for a manual adjustment), optional Batch Number and Expiry Date, and Notes when required.
  3. Check the "Current → New" preview and save.
  4. Open the item (or View movements) to see the last ten movements.

Figure 39.6 — All four ways stock changes go through one method.

On the left are four sources: "Add Item with initial stock", "Adjust Stock dialog 5 manual types", "Receive purchase order" and "Record patient consumption". All four arrows meet at "applyMovement in one transaction". From there a diamond asks "New stock below zero?". "Yes" leads to "400 Insufficient stock". "No" leads to "stock_movements row previous, delta, new" and then to "inventory_items currentStock, nearest expiry", meaning the movement is saved first and the item's quantity and nearest expiry date are then updated.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. Incoming types (transfer in, purchase, initial stock) add; outgoing types (wastage, transfer out, return to supplier, consumption) subtract; a manual adjustment can go either way. Stock may never go below zero. When a batch arrives with an expiry date earlier than the item's current one, the item's expiry date moves to that earlier date. The movement list is the audit trail of stock; there is no other log.

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /inventory/items/:id/adjust-stock → InventoryService.adjustStock → applyMovement inside dataSource.transaction. It loads the item (organization and location), computes the signed delta, refuses a negative result, inserts the stock_movements row (movementType, signed quantity, previousStock, newStock, referenceType, referenceId, batch, expiry, notes, performedBy) and saves the item. The item row is read without a row lock, so two adjustments at the same instant could both read the same starting stock. The controller passes req.user.uuid (the user id) as performedBy. Movement history: the item detail returns the last 10 movements; GET /inventory/items/:id/movements (paged) exists but no screen calls it.

Rules and validations.

  • The dialog allows only MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT, WASTAGE, RETURN_TO_SUPPLIER, TRANSFER_IN, TRANSFER_OUT.
  • Notes are required for manual adjustment and wastage.
  • Quantity must be greater than zero in the dialog; resulting stock must not be negative.
  • Transfers are recorded at one location only; nothing is added at the other location.

Who can do it. inventory.stock.adjust, feature inventory.core. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Writes stock_movements, inventory_items.

Effects on other modules. None (stock is not linked to billing or the consultation).

Error cases. 400 "Notes are required for wastage and manual adjustments"; 400 "Insufficient stock for "Gloves". Available: 3 pieces"; 400 on a disallowed movement type; in the dialog "Enter a quantity greater than zero", "Adjustment would take stock below zero".

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/entities/stock-movement.entity.ts · InventoryService.adjustStock, applyMovement, StockMovementType · web-app/src/features/inventory/components/AdjustStockDialog.tsx

39.3.5 Manage suppliers

Status: [Partial] — works; reachable only through the unlisted /inventory page.

What it does. Keeps the organization's supplier list for purchase orders.

How the user does it.

  1. On the Suppliers tab click Add Supplier, fill the dialog and save.
  2. Use the row menu to edit or deactivate (with a browser confirmation).

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. Suppliers are shared by all locations of the organization; deactivation hides them.

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /suppliers, GET /suppliers, GET /suppliers/:id, PATCH /suppliers/:id, DELETE /suppliers/:id (sets isActive = false) → SupplierService.

Rules and validations. Name required; other fields free text with no format checks.

Who can do it. View: inventory.view; change: inventory.po.manage. Feature inventory.core. Default: Admin manages; Assistant views.

Data read and written. suppliers.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 404 "Supplier not found"; "Name is required" in the dialog.

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/controllers/supplier.controller.ts · SupplierService · web-app/src/features/inventory/components/SuppliersTab.tsx

39.3.6 Raise and track a purchase order

Status: [Unverified] — screens and logic exist; creation stores the user id in purchase_orders.createdBy, which has a foreign key to employees (same risk as 39.3.4). Also, PO numbers are unique across the whole database but numbered per organization, so the second organization's first order in a year would collide (deduced from code).

What it does. Records an order to a supplier with lines, quantities, prices and tax, and moves it through Draft → Ordered.

How the user does it.

  1. On Purchase Orders click Create PO, choose a supplier, add items with Qty and Unit Price, optional Expected Delivery, Tax Rate and Notes, and save. The PO starts as Draft.
  2. Open it and click Mark as Ordered, or Cancel while still a draft.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. The server numbers the order (for example "PO-2026-00001"), computes each line total, the subtotal, the tax and the total.

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /purchase-orders → PurchaseOrderService.create: generatePoNumber takes the organization's latest PO and adds one (PO-<year>-<5 digits>), lines get totalPrice = qty × price rounded to 2 decimals, taxAmount = subtotal × rate / 100. GET /purchase-orders (status and supplier filters, paged), GET /purchase-orders/:id. PATCH /purchase-orders/:id/status checks VALID_PO_TRANSITIONS. DELETE /purchase-orders/:id cancels a draft. poNumber has a unique index over the whole table.

Rules and validations.

  • At least one line in the dialog; ordered quantity ≥ 1; unit price ≥ 0.
  • The sequence continues across years (the counter is not reset), and two orders created at the same moment could get the same number.
  • Line items are not checked to belong to the organization.

Who can do it. View: inventory.view; create and change: inventory.po.manage (implies inventory.view). Feature inventory.core. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Writes purchase_orders, purchase_order_items.

Effects on other modules. None; purchase orders are not linked to expenses or lab payables, and do not appear in the P&L.

Error cases. 400 "Cannot transition purchase order from RECEIVED to ORDERED"; 400 "Only draft purchase orders can be cancelled"; 404 "Purchase order not found"; dialog "Select a supplier", "Add at least one item".

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/services/purchase-order.service.ts · PurchaseOrderService.create, updateStatus, VALID_PO_TRANSITIONS · web-app/src/features/inventory/components/PurchaseOrdersTab.tsx

39.3.7 Receive goods into stock

Status: [Unverified] — goes through the stock-movement path of 39.3.4 with the same foreign-key risk.

What it does. Records quantities that arrived against an ordered PO, adds them to stock with batch and expiry, updates the item's cost price, and sets the PO to Partially Received or Received.

How the user does it.

  1. Open an Ordered or Partial PO and click Receive Items (or Receive More Items).
  2. Enter "Receiving now", Batch # and Expiry per line, and save.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. Each line can be received in several deliveries, but never more than ordered. Each received line adds a "purchase in" movement. When every line is complete the order becomes Received.

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /purchase-orders/:id/receive → PurchaseOrderService.receiveItems in one transaction: per line with quantity > 0, check received + new ≤ ordered, update the PO line, call applyMovement with PURCHASE_IN and reference purchase_order/PO id, and set inventory_items.unitPrice to the line price. Then it recomputes the status from all lines.

Rules and validations.

  • Only from ORDERED or PARTIALLY_RECEIVED.
  • No over-receiving; a zero line is skipped.

Who can do it. inventory.po.manage, feature inventory.core. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. Writes purchase_order_items, purchase_orders, stock_movements, inventory_items.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 400 "Cannot receive items for a purchase order in DRAFT status"; 400 "Cannot receive more than ordered for "…". Ordered: 10, already received: 8"; 404 "Purchase order item … not found"; dialog "Enter at least one quantity to receive".

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/services/purchase-order.service.ts · PurchaseOrderService.receiveItems · web-app/src/features/inventory/components/PurchaseOrdersTab.tsx

39.3.8 Define consumption templates (procedure kits)

Status: [Partial] — templates can be created, edited and deactivated, but nothing on any screen uses them, because the consumption recorder is not placed anywhere.

What it does. Defines a named kit of items and quantities for a procedure, optionally tied to an appointment type for automatic matching.

How the user does it.

  1. On Templates click Add Template, enter name and procedure, optionally an appointment type, add items with quantities and notes, and save.
  2. Edit or deactivate from the row actions.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. A template is a list, not stock; saving it changes no quantities.

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /consumption-templates, GET, GET /consumption-templates/:id, PATCH (replaces all items in one transaction), DELETE (deactivate), GET /consumption-templates/by-type?appointmentType= (first active template for that type) → ConsumptionTemplateService. Items load the inventory item eagerly.

Rules and validations. Name and procedure required; at least one item in the dialog; item quantity ≥ 0.01. Templates are organization-wide, but items belong to one location, so a template made at one location lists that location's items.

Who can do it. View: inventory.view; change: inventory.stock.adjust. Feature inventory.core. Default: Admin.

Data read and written. consumption_templates, consumption_template_items.

Effects on other modules. None.

Error cases. 404 "Consumption template not found"; dialog "Name and procedure are required", "Add at least one item".

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/services/consumption-template.service.ts · ConsumptionTemplateService · web-app/src/features/inventory/components/TemplatesTab.tsx

39.3.9 Record materials used on a patient

Status: [Not implemented] in the web app — the API and a ready component exist, but no screen shows the component. The API path also carries the foreign-key risk of 39.3.4.

What it does. Would record which items were used for a patient (optionally for an appointment or treatment plan), price them at cost, and deduct them from stock.

How the user does it. Not available. ConsumptionRecorder (template picker, "Items Used", "Add Item", Notes) is exported from the inventory feature but imported by no page, including the consultation workspace and the patient record.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. One record per use, with lines priced at the item's current cost; stock goes down in the same transaction, so either everything is saved or nothing is.

Behind the scenes — technically. POST /patient-consumptions → PatientConsumptionService.recordConsumption: per line, load the item at the location, snapshot unitPrice, compute totals, save patient_consumptions with items, then applyMovement with CONSUMPTION and reference appointment, treatment_plan or manual. Read endpoints: GET /patient-consumptions/appointment/:appointmentId, GET /patient-consumptions/patient/:patientId (checks the patient is in the user's scope), GET /patient-consumptions/report?dateFrom&dateTo (top 10 items, total cost, per performer, template versus manual). None of them is called by a screen.

Rules and validations. Quantity ≥ 0.01 per line; stock must not go negative; the treatment-plan id is stored without a foreign key.

Who can do it. Record: inventory.stock.adjust; read: inventory.view. Feature inventory.core.

Data read and written. patient_consumptions, patient_consumption_items, stock_movements, inventory_items.

Effects on other modules. None today (not billed, not shown on the encounter).

Error cases. 404 "Inventory item … not found"; 400 "Insufficient stock…".

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/services/patient-consumption.service.ts · PatientConsumptionService.recordConsumption · web-app/src/features/inventory/components/ConsumptionRecorder.tsx

39.3.10 Daily low-stock and expiry alerts

Status: [Partial] — the job runs and counts, but only writes a warning to the server log; no user is notified.

What it does. Once a day finds items that are low or expiring at each location where both inventory features are on.

How the user does it. Switch on inventory.alerts (and inventory.core) in Features. Nothing appears for users; the counts go to the server log only.

Behind the scenes — in simple terms. Every morning the server checks each location's stock. A notification for users is planned in a code comment but not built.

Behind the scenes — technically. InventoryAlertService.checkAlerts, @Cron('0 8 * * *'), every day at 08:00 server time (not the location's timezone), in the process that runs scheduled jobs (worker or all-in-one). For each organization–location pair with active items it checks both features, calls getLowStockItems and getExpiringItems (30 days) and logs "[Inventory Alerts] org=… location=… lowStock=… expiringSoon=…". A TODO notes that in-app notifications should go to members holding inventory.view.

Rules and validations. Fixed 30-day window; out-of-stock items are not counted as low.

Who can do it. The job, no user. Feature inventory.alerts (no permission belongs to it).

Data read and written. Reads inventory_items. Writes nothing.

Effects on other modules. None; the notifications module (Chapter 44) receives nothing.

Error cases. None visible to users.

Technical references: backend/src/inventory/services/inventory-alerts.service.ts · InventoryAlertService.checkAlerts · none

39.4 Entities and data model

Figure 39.7 — The inventory tables and their links.

The diagram centres on inventory_items (id, organizationId, locationId, categoryId, currentStock, reorderLevel, expiryDate). Above it, inventory_categories "groups" items. Left, stock_movements (inventoryItemId, performedBy, movementType, quantity, newStock, referenceId) records how items "are changed"; employees "performs" movements and "creates" purchase_orders (supplierId, createdBy, poNumber, status, totalAmount), which suppliers "supplies". purchase_orders "contains" purchase_order_items (purchaseOrderId, inventoryItemId, orderedQuantity, receivedQuantity), each pointing to an item. Right, consumption_templates "lists" consumption_template_items (each a kit part pointing to an item); patients are "used on" patient_consumptions (patientId, appointmentId, templateId, performedBy, totalCost), which may be "based on" a template and "contains" patient_consumption_items, each pointing to an item.

The relationships in words (columns are camelCase in this module, unlike most of the Platform):

  • Each item belongs to one organization and one location; deleting either deletes its items (CASCADE). An item may have a category; deleting the category sets it to NULL.
  • Each stock movement belongs to one item (deleting the item deletes its movements, CASCADE) and names one employee in performedBy (FK to employees, NO ACTION). referenceType + referenceId point to the cause (purchase order, appointment, treatment plan, manual) without a foreign key; referenceId is text.
  • Suppliers and categories belong to the organization (CASCADE), not to a location.
  • Each purchase order belongs to one organization and location (CASCADE), one supplier and one creating employee (both NO ACTION). Its lines are deleted with it (CASCADE); each line points to one item.
  • Each template belongs to the organization (CASCADE); its items are deleted with it (CASCADE) and point to items.
  • Each patient consumption belongs to an organization, location and patient (CASCADE), optionally to an appointment (SET NULL) and a template (SET NULL); treatmentPlanId has no foreign key. Its lines are deleted with it (CASCADE).
  • Quantities and prices are decimal(10,2) numeric columns in rupees, not paisa.
  • A legacy entity inventory (snake_case columns item_name, quantity, unit_price) exists in the code but is registered by no module, so the running API never creates or uses it.

39.5 Status lifecycles

Figure 39.8 — The purchase order status map from VALID_PO_TRANSITIONS.

A purchase order enters at DRAFT through POST /purchase-orders. From DRAFT, "PATCH status ORDERED" leads to ORDERED (setting the order date), and "DELETE or PATCH status" leads to CANCELLED. From ORDERED, "POST receive, some lines short" leads to PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, "POST receive, all lines full" leads to RECEIVED, and "PATCH status, API only" leads to CANCELLED. From PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, "POST receive, all lines full" leads to RECEIVED and "PATCH status, API only" to CANCELLED. RECEIVED and CANCELLED are final. The screen offers cancel only for drafts; cancelling an ordered PO is possible only through the API, and cancelling a partly received PO does not reverse stock already received. A manual status change to RECEIVED is also allowed by the map without receiving any goods.

Stock movements have no lifecycle; they are written once and never changed. Their eight types are: INITIAL_STOCK, PURCHASE_IN, TRANSFER_IN (add), CONSUMPTION, WASTAGE, TRANSFER_OUT, RETURN_TO_SUPPLIER (subtract) and MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT (either way).

39.6 Connections to other modules

  • Access control (Chapter 57). Three permissions (inventory.view, inventory.stock.adjust, inventory.po.manage) belong to the feature inventory.core.
  • Patients and Appointments (Chapters 28–29). Patient consumptions point to patients and appointments; no screen uses this yet.
  • Consultation (Chapter 31). Not connected: the consultation workspace does not record materials.
  • Billing and Reports (Chapters 34, 36). Not connected: billable items, purchase orders and consumption costs appear in no invoice, expense or report.
  • Notifications (Chapter 44). Not connected: the alert job only logs.

39.7 Limitations and known gaps

  • No sidebar entry; /inventory is reachable only by address.
  • Stock movements, purchase orders and patient consumptions store the user id in columns that reference employees; this is expected to fail at the database (not tested).
  • PO numbers are globally unique but generated per organization, so they can collide between organizations; the counter does not reset each year and is not safe against simultaneous creation.
  • No category management screen and no default categories.
  • Consumption recording, consumption reports and the full movement history have no screen.
  • Alerts are log-only and use the server's time and date.
  • Stock changes do not lock the item row.
  • Transfers do not move stock to the other location.
  • Inventory costs do not reach the P&L, expenses or patient invoices.
  • The tabs use plain tables without card view, and confirmations use the browser's dialog.

39.8 Owner's FAQ

How do staff open Inventory? Only by typing /inventory; there is no sidebar item. Adding one means adding an entry to the navigation registry.

Can stock go negative? No. Any movement that would take stock below zero is refused with "Insufficient stock".

Can I see who changed a quantity? Yes, in principle: every change is a stock movement with the before and after quantity, type, notes and the person. The item sheet shows the last ten.

Does receiving a purchase order create an expense or a lab bill? No. Purchase orders are not linked to billing or the P&L.

Will the system warn me about low stock? Not on screen. The daily 08:00 job writes counts to the server log only. The Low Stock tile and filter on the page show the current state.

Are suppliers per branch? No. Suppliers, categories and templates are shared by the whole organization; items, stock and purchase orders are per location.

Can an Assistant change stock? Not with the default role: the Assistant can only view.

Where is stock stored? In inventory_items.currentStock, kept equal to the newStock of the latest movement in stock_movements.

Chapter 40 — Dental Lab

This chapter describes the clinic side of dental-lab work on the Platform: how a clinic keeps a list of the dental labs it works with, how it orders crowns, bridges and dentures from them, follows the work through try-ins and shipments, and approves or sends back what comes home. It is written for the product owner, who needs to know exactly what the module does today and where it stops. "Lab" here always means a dental laboratory that makes prosthetics, never a diagnostic test lab. The lab's own screens (the lab portal and the no-login magic link page) are in Chapter 41, and the money side (patient lab invoices, vendor bills, payments, statements) is in Chapter 42.

40.1 What this module is for

A dental clinic rarely makes crowns, bridges and dentures itself. It sends a lab order to a lab, the lab makes the work in stages, ships it back, and the clinic fits it on the patient. This module covers that whole case from the clinic's chair:

  • Lab list. The clinic chooses which labs it works with. Each connection is a lab link that carries payment terms and how much of the patient's identity the lab may see.
  • Lab price list. For every service a linked lab offers, the clinic sees what the lab charges it and what it charges the patient, and maps each lab service to one of its own billable treatments.
  • Order templates. A doctor saves "my usual zirconia crown" once and starts later orders from it.
  • Lab orders. One order is one case for one patient with one or more lab order items (a crown, a bridge). The order is a draft until submitted. At submit, prices and form answers are frozen. After submit, changes are revisions, never overwrites.
  • Lab access. The lab can answer through the lab portal, through a magic link (a no-login web page the clinic sends by message) or, when the lab does not answer at all, a lab coordinator at the clinic can record the lab's answer on its behalf.
  • Production. Work moves through the lab's stages. Try-in rounds go to the clinic and back. The clinic receives parcels, approves or rejects them, delivers the finished item and, if needed, asks for a remake.

Who uses it, by canonical role:

  • Doctor. Creates and submits orders, answers the lab's questions, decides try-ins, approves or rejects work, delivers it. Sees orders they ordered or created (scope own).
  • Receptionist and Assistant. Can view the lab orders of their location and receive shipments at the front desk. They cannot create or change orders.
  • Admin and the owner. Everything, including the lab list, the lab price list, shared templates and acting for a lab.
  • Accountant. No lab-order access; the Accountant holds the lab billing and payables permissions that Chapter 42 covers.
  • Super admin. Maintains the platform lab directory, the lab members and each lab's services and prices.

Where it appears in the sidebar (labels from nav.registry.ts, all inside the Clinic section by default): Labs (/labs, needs lab.links.manage), Lab orders (/lab-orders, needs lab.orders.view), Lab price list (/lab-catalog, needs lab.catalog.manage) and Order templates (/lab-order-templates, needs lab.orders.create). Lab billing and Lab payables also sit there and belong to Chapter 42. A Lab portal entry appears only for users who are lab members. For the super admin there is Lab Directory (/lab-directory) in the Admin section.

The clinic side sits behind the feature dental.lab_orders (display name "Lab Management"). It is not enabled by default: the super admin entitles it to an organization and the owner switches it on. The platform routes (directory, catalog) ignore it, and so do the lab portal routes, because a lab is not a tenant.

How the lab order runs on the workflow engine

A lab order, each lab order item and each try-in stage round have a status. These statuses are not fixed in code. Each one is a state of a workflow template (a versioned definition of states and transitions that the super admin edits in Config Studio; Chapter 43 covers the engine). When a draft order is created it pins the newest published order workflow of its specialty, and every item it contains pins an item workflow. Later edits to a template never change cases already in flight. Every status change goes through one engine call, which locks the row, finds the (state, action) pair in the pinned version, checks the actor's side (clinic, lab or system) and role, checks a required reason or input, writes the new state, writes the status history and then runs the transition's effects.

The default dental templates are seeded as published version 1 (DENTAL_ORDER, DENTAL_ITEM, DENTAL_STAGE). The state diagrams in section 40.5 show those seeded definitions. An organization that has published its own version would see different states, and nothing in this chapter would describe them. The labels in the web app are a lookup table for the seeded codes; an unknown code is shown with its underscores replaced by spaces.

One rule is in code, not in data: the order's status follows its items. After every item change the engine recomputes the order status in the same transaction, using fixed rules (first match wins): all items cancelled gives cancelled; a manual hold gives on hold; ignoring items that left the work (cancelled, rejected, remake required), all items approved or delivered gives completed; all received or later gives under review; some received gives partially received; all ready or dispatched gives ready; some ready gives partially ready; any in production, at clinic try-in or in QC gives in progress; all accepted gives accepted; otherwise submitted. The statuses draft, clarification needed, rejected by lab, cancelled and completed are never overwritten by this derivation, except that a remake reopens a completed order.
